---
title: "Direct source-basis ln K observations in joint fitting"
format: html
execute:
  enabled: false
---

A direct observation of a named reaction's source-basis ln K at fixed positive
temperature can enter `epcsaft.regression.fit` jointly with an equilibrium
observation. The direct value and first coefficient derivatives use the stored
reaction correlation without an equilibrium solve or EOS reference transfer.
All 24 direct derivative comparisons are exact in the tested floating-point
values. A manufactured three-temperature ln K series plus one bubble-pressure
observation recovers a and b with errors 2.27×10⁻¹¹ and 4.08×10⁻⁹ K,
respectively, with covariance rank two. These are numerical verification
results, not physical validation or application parameter adoption.

## Quantity, basis and fitting method

[Issue #211](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/211) supplies the
accepted question and +25 net runtime-line amendment. The
[equation owner](../../engine/docs/equations.md#source_log_equilibrium_constant_observation)
and [ALG-FIT](../../engine/docs/science/algorithms.md#alg-fit) define

$$
y_r(T)=\ln K_{src,r}(T)=a_r+b_r/T+c_r\ln(T/T_{ref,r})+d_rT,
\qquad \phi(T)=(1,1/T,\ln(T/T_{ref}),T).
$$

The units of a, b, c and d are 1, K, 1 and K⁻¹. The exact derivative is
φ for that named reaction's coordinates, zero for other reactions and EOS
coordinates. Scalar K uses ln K and admits only the a coordinate. The source
record and Tref remain fixed; a referenced source observation does not contain
the reference contraction used by the equilibrium calculation. Naming, tying
and fixed-target rejection remain with the #187 coordinate owner.

Use `ObservationKind.LogEquilibriumConstant`, the reaction name in `reaction`
and the fixed positive temperature in `problem.temperature.value`. Only
Difference residuals are admitted because ln K is already logarithmic.
The existing Difference residual, affine optimizer chart, weights and covariance
chain remain unchanged. With scale=1, a standard uncertainty σ in ln K uses
weight=1/σ². Reported covariance is conditional on independent errors, local
linearization, full rank and an interior solution; the manufactured data have
no measured uncertainty or model discrepancy.

## Exact value and derivative identities

The [native falsifier](../../engine/tests/native/regression_checks.cpp)
uses the existing three-species, two-reaction neutral input. The first source
law is a=0.4, b=80 K, c=0.5, d=0.001 K⁻¹, Tref=300 K, valid 150–400 K.
One active EOS segment count is interleaved with all four coefficients and
the other reaction's scalar a. Reversing reaction declaration order at each
temperature falsifies positional lookup. Physical derivative rows remain EOS
first, followed by reaction coordinates in their declaration order.

| T, K | ∂y/∂a | ∂y/∂b, K⁻¹ | ∂y/∂c | ∂y/∂d, K | Largest absolute column error |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 200 | 1 | 0.005 | −0.40546510810816444 | 200 | 0 |
| 250 | 1 | 0.004 | −0.1823215567939546 | 250 | 0 |
| 300 | 1 | 0.0033333333333333335 | 0 | 300 | 0 |
| 350 | 1 | 0.002857142857142857 | 0.15415067982725836 | 350 | 0 |

Both the EOS and other-reaction columns equal zero exactly at all four T.
The four polynomial value comparisons also have zero absolute error. A
referenced H₂O⇌Na⁺+Cl⁻ source at 298.15 K returns ln(10⁻⁸)=−18.420680743952367
without converting to its density-basis constant. A scalar K input is likewise
observed as ln K. These exact finite identities qualify the stated calculation,
not arbitrary chemistry or second derivatives.

[comparisons.csv](results/comparisons.csv) retains each numerical operand,
temperature and criterion once. Tables are sufficient here: the comparison is
an exact coefficient lookup at four temperatures with zero errors, rather than
a sampled continuous prediction or an uncertainty distribution. A curve would
not clarify the identity.

## Joint a/b recovery

The manufactured methane–ethane bubble fixture comes from #187's native input.
Its reaction `iso` has a=−5.172888631054627, b=300 K, c=0.5, d=0.001 K⁻¹,
Tref=200 K and a 150–220 K window. Independent direct values are formed from
that declared formula at 170, 180 and 190 K. The 180 K bubble-pressure value
is generated by the existing equilibrium owner at the same known coefficients.
Each observation then receives the same displaced start, a+0.1 and b−20 K.
The fitted a/b scales are 1 and 180 K. Direct rows use unit scale, Difference
and unit weight; the bubble-pressure row keeps its existing LogRatio form.
Other coefficients, EOS parameters and source declarations are fixed.

| Coefficient | Known | Recovered | Absolute error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| a | −5.172888631054627 | −5.1728886310319 | 2.2726709403286804×10⁻¹¹ |
| b, K | 300 | 299.99999999592046 | 4.07953848480247×10⁻⁹ |

The existing recovery criteria are absolute 10⁻⁶ for a and relative 10⁻⁶ for b.
The final half-squared weighted cost is 1.5977348223734068×10⁻²⁴, below 10⁻¹⁴.
There are zero failed trials, six recorded iterations, and available conditional
covariance with asserted rank two. This demonstrates local noise-free recovery;
it does not establish global identifiability for experimental joint datasets.
The installed Python numerical check separately recovers a=−1.5 and b=150 K
from negative ln K values and verifies the exact optimizer columns after
absolute weights 4, 9 and 16. It establishes that the exposed observation kind
and reaction name reach the same native fitting calculation.

## Named rejection and verification limits

With only an EOS coordinate fitted, direct observation admission still rejects
the observed reaction `reaction_a` by name for affinity targets, dependent
reaction sets, supplied standard Gibbs values and K fixed by thermochemistry.
[summary.json](results/summary.json) retains all four messages and joint-fit
diagnostics. The 39 new native comparisons pass; the baseline bubble fixture
also checks its pinned pressure and compositions before recovery.

The current non-editable wheel was built and installed before these numerical
checks. The native `regression_fit` program passed in 42.85 s. `check-all.sh`
passed 109 Python numerical checks, six fast native programs, equation registry,
measured budgets, retained-data layout, architecture, Ruff and mypy. Runtime
counts are Regression 1484 (+21), Bindings 1723 (+2), Python 2357 (+2), total
18830 (+25); all other runtime layers are unchanged. Hard ceilings were amended
to the measured Regression, Python and aggregate counts; Bindings stays within
its existing ceiling. The wheel SHA-256 and base `95ba231e` are retained in the
summary. Heavy calculations used the shared lock, finite wall-time limits,
priority 10, one OpenMP/BLAS thread and two requested build jobs.

Independent GPT-6.1 Sol high cse:review returned **Supported**, with no required
corrections, for scientific commit `158df58fef21a083def9ff8c6babeae5fdde3291`
against `95ba231e`. The reviewer independently confirmed the value/derivative
owners, retained results, registry, wheel identity and +25 net runtime count,
and replayed the installed Python recovery and weighted columns. The later
documentation commit records this verdict only; it changes no calculation or
retained numerical operand. This notebook remains unpromoted for manuscript use. Only first parameter derivatives at fixed declared T are qualified.
No EOS reference conversion of the direct data, coefficient Hessian,
application calibration, physical validation or parameter adoption is claimed.
